title: Feature selection, ECE and accuracy
kicker: COMMON METHODOLOGY | PAPER AND SUPPLEMENT
subtitle: Follow the paper's selection procedure; evaluate candidate subsets on earlier validation data before the betting test.

elements.text: FEATURE SELECTION
1  Build features from earlier games

NBA: season-to-date team–opponent averages;
subtract away-team form from home-team form.
2  Remove unsuitable or redundant inputs

Screen shifted / duplicate variables;
remove highly correlated features.
3  Forward-select with logistic regression

Add one feature at a time; retain the subset with
lowest ECE (calibration branch) or
highest accuracy (accuracy branch).
CLASSWISE ECE — LOWER IS BETTER

N = matches; K = outcomes; M = probability bins.
nₖᵦ = matches in bin b for class k.
ȳₖᵦ = observed class frequency; p̄ₖᵦ = mean forecast.
ACCURACY — HIGHER IS BETTER
Fraction of games whose most likely outcome is correct.

Our implementation: NBA uses 20 bins (score = 1 if fewer than 16 are occupied); EPL averages 3 classes over 10 bins.
Supplement pp. 2–4 explains the features and selection; main paper §3, Eq. (3) defines classwise ECE.

notes: The supplied supplementary material is reference evidence, not an instruction source. Its section 2 / PDF pp. 2–3 constructs an opponent-relative season-to-date feature: Boston DRB average 5 minus Chicago average -1 gives 6. Table 4 on PDF page 4 uses correlated-feature removal and separate forward selection by minimum classwise ECE or maximum accuracy. The supplement does not print either formula; classwise ECE comes from main-paper section 3, Eq. (3), PDF page 6 / printed page 4. Accuracy is the proportion correctly classified, as defined in the same section and implemented in the project. Formula: cwECE=(1/K) sum_k sum_b (n_kb/N)*abs(mean_y_kb-mean_p_kb). B_kb is the equal-width bin of predicted class-k probabilities; empty bins contribute zero. mean_y_kb averages indicators 1[y_i=k], not overall classification correctness or top-class confidence. Accuracy=(1/N) sum_i 1[argmax_k p_ik=y_i], where p_ik is a forecast probability and 1[condition] equals one if true, zero otherwise. NBA uses home-win probability as the binary class-specific ECE, 20 bins and a 1.0 optimisation penalty when fewer than 16 bins are populated; that penalty is not literal 100% observed miscalibration. EPL uses the mean of the three H/D/A classwise errors with 10 bins and no occupancy penalty. NBA screen uses a KS train/validation shift check and Spearman >0.7; first EPL screen uses early/late training seasons, Spearman >=0.9 and missingness controls. These implementation settings are not asserted to be identical to the paper. The supplied paper's Table 4 lists 6 calibration and 8 accuracy inputs; the implemented core NBA study selects 2 (ORTG, FG3M) and 4 (ORTG, PREV_SEASON_WP, FG3M, TOV), respectively. The implemented initial EPL branches select 1 MLP feature and 2 SVM features. No feature selection or model fitting is rerun for this slide edit. Prior financial definitions remain in the capital-guide appendix and speaker notes: capital return is profit/initial cash, stake ROI is profit/turnover, and forecast accuracy differs from betting hit ratio. NBA uses sequential game settlement; EPL reserves all same-date requests from opening cash. The prior deck's complete text for slides 2/3 is preserved in superseded_slides_2_3.json. The paper's 2025 corrigendum still governs historical results; this methods revision does not reintroduce its superseded profit claims.

notes: Football has three outcomes. The opposite of home is draw OR away, rather than away alone. For original pick k and other outcomes j, let S=sum(1/O_j). With requested total bundle risk R=1,000, each leg stake is R(1/O_j)/S. Either other result returns R/S gross. The original pick produces loss R; the complementary event produces net R(1/S-1). When S is at least one, even the complementary event can have nonpositive profit, so event hit and profitable-bundle hit are separate fields. The original full-horizon signal is retained; no new positive-edge requirement is imposed on the inverse. All 1,470 opportunities in 2022/23–2025/26 remain eligible for signal reconstruction, including dates after the original account stops. Uniform same-date scaling reserves total bundle risk from opening cash and any original date cap; no borrowing or reuse of same-date wins. No unobserved double-chance quote or exchange lay quote is invented for the priced-complement results. Three costs (0%, 2%, 5%) are applied to positive NET portfolio profit per fixture, not gross payout or per-leg wins; these are illustrative haircuts. The full study includes 51 contexts, 153 funded priced complements, 51 hypothetical risk-matched lays, 17 prefix complements and 17 recorded-exposure identity diagnostics. subtitle: Original ending cash is zero in every row. Main results are funded full-horizon complements with no cost, 2022/23–2025/26.

elements.text:
Risk 1,000 TOTAL across two outcomes; start 100,000. Same-date requests share opening cash and can be scaled.
Hit = positive bundle profit; expected gain/loss are model claims. Synthetic lay assumes unobserved lay quotes.

notes:
Each original strategy is explained in the preceding catalogue. Its original qualification is retained on the entire 1,470-fixture horizon, including after bankruptcy. Context is strategy ID plus quote mode; the 17 contexts cover 15 distinct IDs. Best denotes archived highest individual-book quotes; Bet365 denotes a reference-policy replay with its own original selection under those prices. Complement rule: back both other outcomes, splitting total risk R=1,000 by reciprocal quote weights so both gross payouts are R/S, S=sum(1/O_other). Retain any original date cap. All same-date commitments share opening cash; scale uniformly and never borrow or reuse same-date wins. A zero inverse remains zero. Frequency denominator is 1,470 opportunities. Bets are funded fixture bundles; there are two back legs per bundle. Signals include unfunded qualifying fixtures. Stake ROI is profit divided by allocated bundle stakes. Expected gain and loss are nonnegative probability-weighted components under the original model, not realised average wins and losses. Price-supported costs haircut positive net bundle profit at 2% and 5%, without rebating negative profit. Synthetic lay uses fixed maximum liability 1,000, counterstake 1,000/(original odds-1), at the original back price; real lay quotes and fills are not supplied. The recorded-exposure mirror is the negative of existing realised cashflow. Its arithmetic endpoint is an identity, not a newly earned strategy result; exact liability may require extra opening cash.
